topic: How do interference mitigation techniques adapt when handling tunneled versus non-tunneled traffic in multi-beam satellite systems?
response: Interference mitigation techniques in multibeam satellite systems employ frequency band separation and orthogonal polarizations to minimize intercell interference.  This aims to reduce signal degradation and maintain optimal SINR (Signal-to-Noise Ratio). 4 subbands are commonly used, ensuring disjoint frequency bands for adjacent beams.
reference_context: In multibeam satellite systems, the transmit signal is partially radiated to adjacent beams through antenna sidlobes.  This creates interference that affects communication links. To mitigate this, operators utilize frequency band separation and orthogonal polarizations.
